# Practical Exercise: A screening experiment 


## Aims of this practical exercise


In this exercise you will:

- see a screening experiment in action.

## Before you undertake this exercise...


Get the necessary add-on packages:


## Coils experiment

This experiment was conducted to minimise the scrap rate, measured by the reject percentage.


Process parameters	| Labels	| Low level	| High level
--- | --- | --- | --- 
Felt lubrication	| A	| Dry	| Soaked
Wire diameter	| B	| 0.75 mm	| 0.76 mm
Friction on pulley	| C	| Low	| High
Brake tension	| D	| 1.5 kg	| 2 kg
Winding width	| E	| High	| Low
Dirt buildup	| F	| Unclean	| Clean
Axial start position	| G	| A	| B


``` {r}
Coils = read.csv("Coils.csv") |>
glimpse()
```

## Required

Q: Find the significant factors for this experiment.
```{r}
model <- lm(Rejects ~ A*B*C*D*E*F*G, data = Coils)
aliases(model)
anova(model)
```

```{r}
DanielPlot((model), half = TRUE)

```

```{r, fig.width=20}
effects <- coef(model)[-1]
effects_clean <- effects[!is.na(effects)]

# Generate Lenth plot
BsMD::LenthPlot(effects_clean, yaxt = "n", ylab = "effects")

```


```{r}
null_model <- lm(Rejects ~ 1, data = Coils)

# Perform forward stepwise selection
summary(step(null_model, scope = ~ A*B*C*D*E*F*G, direction = "forward", trace = 0))
```
```{r}
summary(null_model)
```


```{r}
model2 <- lm(Rejects~ B*D*G, data = Coils)
anova(model2)
coef(model2)
summary(model2)
```

```{r}
MEPlot(model2)
```

```{r}
IAPlot(model2)
```

```{r}
BsMD::LenthPlot(model2)
```

```{r}
DanielPlot((model2), half = TRUE)
```

No significant factors. 


Q: What if you are a little more conservative given this is ascreening experiment. Relax the significance level to 10% and determine which factors hsould be further examined.
```{r}
BsMD::LenthPlot(model2, alpha = 0.10)
```

```{r}
DanielPlot(model2, alpha = 0.20)
```

still no change. 

Q: Given your findings, what do you recommend for the settings of the factors?
Nothing really matters, need more data. 

Try wire diameter high and brake tension anda xial start point low.
